questions.q: 'The ground is wet — it ___ have rained last night.'
questions.a: 'must' — confident deduction from present evidence about a past event. A wrong answer 'should' reveals the student confuses deduction with advisability — the two functions share no overlap but students collapse them.

questions.q: Correct the error: 'You should had apologised.'
questions.a: 'should have apologised' — modal perfect needs 'have', never 'had'. A wrong answer keeping 'had' or changing to 'should apologised' shows the student doesn't know the fixed modal+have+V3 template.

questions.q: 'He ___ have caught the train, but he left late.'
questions.a: 'could' — unrealized past ability/opportunity. A wrong answer 'must' or 'should' shows the student cannot yet map speaker stance (lost chance) onto the modal — the expressive core of this node.

questions.q: Modal + have + past participle talks about a past that didn't happen or a past we deduce: 'should have studied' = regret/reproach, 'must have left' = confident deduction, 'could have won' = unrealized ability, 'might have forgotten' = weak past ______.

Fill in the blank: Modal + have + past participle talks about a past that didn't happen or a past we deduce: 'should have studied' = regret/reproach, 'must have left' = confident deduction, 'could have won' = unrealized ability, 'might have forgotten' = weak past ______.
Fill in the blank: Three past scenarios on the board: (1) 'The lights are off — they ___ have gone out' → ______ → 'must'.
Fill in the blank: Three past scenarios on the board: (______) 'The lights are off — they ___ have gone out' → deduction → 'must'.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student correctly deploys should have/must have/could have/might have for regret, deduction, and unrealized possibility, and distinguishes deduction-must from obligation-must.
